      <title>Collision of two trains in Egypt kills at least seven</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/08/egypt-two-trains-deadly-collision</link>
      <description><p>President orders prompt investigation after one train derails in collision in al-Ayyat about 50km from Cairo</p><p>Seven people were killed and at least 125 injured when two trains collided on Sunday south of the Egyptian capital, Cairo, officials said.</p><p>The crash occurred in al-Ayyat district in Giza province, about 50km (30 miles) south of Cairo, when a train travelling to Fayoum province crashed into the rear of a train heading to the southern province of Aswan, according to the transport ministry.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/08/egypt-two-trains-deadly-collision">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Kenyan doomsday sect leader jailed for 200 years for murder of 190 children</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/06/kenyan-doomsday-sect-leader-jailed-murders-paul-mackenzie</link>
      <description><p>Paul Mackenzie convicted over deaths of children and one adult after followers were ordered to starve themselves and their families</p><p>The leader of a Kenyan doomsday sect has been sentenced to 200 years in prison for the murders of 190 children and one adult in one of the world’s worst cult disasters in recent history.</p><p>The sentence, comprising 100 years for murder by starvation and 100 years by direct homicide, came two weeks after the court in Kenya’s coastal city of Mombasa <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/19/kenya-starvation-cult-leader-guilty-murder-190-children">found the cult leader guilty</a> of the crimes.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/06/kenyan-doomsday-sect-leader-jailed-murders-paul-mackenzie">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>ANC faces bruising defeat in South African local elections with 80% of ballots counted</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/06/anc-faces-defeat-south-african-local-elections</link>
      <description><p>Former liberation movement’s share of national vote almost 14 percentage points below 2021 result</p><p>The African National Congress is on course to suffer a bruising defeat in South Africa’s local elections, with the once dominant party of Nelson Mandela falling to under a third of the vote nationally with more than 80% of ballots counted.</p><p>Wednesday’s fragmented vote marks another stage in the decline of the ANC, which has led national governments since the end of white minority apartheid rule in 1994. High unemployment, crime, corruption and poor local service delivery have all contributed to <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/04/anc-south-africa-local-elections-water-outages-power-cuts">voters turning away from the party</a>.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/06/anc-faces-defeat-south-african-local-elections">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Patient is ⁠in ​stable condition and will be transferred to a specialist ‘high consequence’ infectious disease unit</p><p>A British healthcare worker with Ebola is being evacuated from the Democratic Republic of the Congo to the UK for medical treatment, it has been confirmed.</p><p>“A British citizen currently in the DR Congo has tested positive for Ebola,” a spokesperson for the UK government said in a statement on Wednesday. “The UK has well-established procedures for dealing with cases like this, and those processes have been activated … The risk to the UK public from Ebola remains low.”</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/04/british-healthcare-worker-ebola-evacuated-drc-to-uk-document-shows">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Violent storms lash northern Iraq and parts of Iran, while Portugal faces strong winds and Japan braces for further snowfall</p><p>Deadly flash floods hit northern Iraq on Saturday as severe thunderstorms swept across the region, including in neighbouring Iran. The city of Erbil, in Iraq, was particularly badly hit, with extensive damage to homes and businesses. Streets were inundated as torrential rain fell over a short period.</p><p>Rainfall exceeded forecasts, with an estimated 80mm falling in the city, compared with expectations of 30mm.       <title>Pope’s visit to Argentina sets up showdown with ‘hyper-capitalist’ Milei</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/08/popes-visit-to-argentina-sets-up-showdown-with-hyper-capitalist-milei</link>
      <description><p>President has opposing views on many issues, and once called Leo’s predecessor the ‘representative of the Evil One’</p><p>Trees are being planted in the garden. The brightly coloured buildings are getting another coat of paint. The choir rehearses. Hundreds of other residents, several of them using wheelchairs, practise their positions outside the sanctuary. Excitement is in the air, because on Monday 9 November, the Cottolengo Don Orione – a Catholic-run home for disabled people – will be the first stop on Pope Leo XIV’s first full day of his trip to Argentina.</p><p>But the pope’s visit to Claypole, about 26km from Buenos Aires, does not come at an especially happy time for the home, which counts about 400 residents with disabilities. Argentina’s president, Javier Milei, has made wide-ranging cuts to disability funding.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/08/popes-visit-to-argentina-sets-up-showdown-with-hyper-capitalist-milei">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/09/russians-killed-ukraine-war-leaked-data</link>
      <description><p>Hacked death records reveal scale of losses since Moscow launched full-scale invasion nearly five years ago</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/09/ukraine-war-briefing-post-war-security-guarantees-a-key-focus-in-upcoming-abu-dhabi-talks-says-rubio">Ukraine war briefing: post war ‘security guarantees’ a key focus in upcoming Abu Dhabi talks, says Rubio</a></p></li><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2026/nov/09/polands-krakow-attack-ukraine-russia-france-germany-europe-latest-news">Europe live – latest updates</a></p></li></ul><p>More than 400,000 Russians have been killed fighting in Ukraine since Moscow launched its full-scale invasion nearly five years ago, according to leaked data from the country’s state statistics agency, Rosstat.</p><p>The data, obtained by the Belarusian opposition-linked hacker group Cyber Partisans and the Ukrainian hacking collective Silent Crow, contains more than 11 million death certificates, including details of the deceased’s age, place of residence and location of death.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/09/russians-killed-ukraine-war-leaked-data">Continue reading...</a></description>

<rss version="2.0" xmlns:atom="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom" xmlns:media="http://search.yahoo.com/mrss/" xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/"><channel><language>en</language><title>Latest news reports on FRANCE, French politics and culture - France 24</title><description>Follow FRANCE 24’s coverage of events in Paris and across France, Corsica and the French overseas territories. An insider look at French politics, culture, society, technology and sport through on-the-ground reports, investigations, exclusive interviews, debates and analyses.</description><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/</link><lastBuildDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 15:10:20 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.france24.com/en/france/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>France</category><title>French PM brings forward 1.6% increase in minimum wage in bid to calm protests</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261109-french-pm-lecornu-announces-increase-minimum-wage-bid-to-calm-protests</link><description>
French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu announced on Monday that a planned 1.6% increase in the minimum wage would be brought forward from January to December after holding talks with trade unions and business leaders over the cost-of-living crisis that has fuelled weeks of unrest across France. The increase fell well short of the demands of unions, which have called for fresh protests in the coming days.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23136886-dc33-11f1-b2ff-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6WB27W.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23136886-dc33-11f1-b2ff-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6WB27W.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">f6ee1d4e-dc43-11f1-9280-633626f68692</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 13:52:34 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23136886-dc33-11f1-b2ff-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6WB27W.jpg">© Kenzo Tribouillard, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Controversial West African activist Kemi Seba detained in Paris</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20241015-controversial-west-african-activist-kemi-seba-detained-in-paris</link><description>
Kemi Seba, a controversial African activist known for his virulent anti-Western stance, has been arrested in Paris, a source close to the case told AFP Tuesday.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d792557e-8afa-11ef-b7b5-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000_1U53IC.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d792557e-8afa-11ef-b7b5-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000_1U53IC.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b9cb5c02-8aff-11ef-811f-005056a97652</guid><pubDate>Tue, 15 Oct 2024 14:17:13 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d792557e-8afa-11ef-b7b5-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000_1U53IC.jpg">© Stéphane de Sakutin, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France’s new health pass rules raise questions as many scramble to adapt</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20210714-france-s-new-health-pass-rules-raise-questions-as-many-scramble-to-adapt</link><description>
While the extension of France’s health pass and other new anti-Covid 19 measures announced by President Emmanuel Macron Monday night are yet to be hammered out in detail, what’s certain is that a full-throttled return to a normal life of frequenting café terraces, restaurants, cinemas, theatres and other culture and leisure activities will now hinge on having a pass sanitaire (or health pass).
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/95a7a1f4-e018-11eb-931e-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/61be21e7dd8409eb6f2604b7d2e8d59f8e2865dc.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/95a7a1f4-e018-11eb-931e-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/61be21e7dd8409eb6f2604b7d2e8d59f8e2865dc.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">5823e86e-e4b0-11eb-8c07-005056bf762b</guid><pubDate>Wed, 14 Jul 2021 16:03:14 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/95a7a1f4-e018-11eb-931e-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/61be21e7dd8409eb6f2604b7d2e8d59f8e2865dc.jpg">© Sameer Al-Doumy, AFP</source><dc:creator>Romain BRUNET</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Daughter loses legal case in bitter Asterix family feud</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/20131211-daughter-loses-legal-case-bitter-asterix-family-feud-france-comics</link><description>A long-running family feud between Asterix co-creator Albert Uderzo and his daughter took a new twist on Tuesday after judges dismissed a claim by Sylvie Uderzo that her father was mentally frail and being exploited.</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/abe23e78-093f-11e9-b87e-005056a964fe/w:1024/p:16x9/asterix_0.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/abe23e78-093f-11e9-b87e-005056a964fe/w:1024/p:16x9/asterix_0.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">563894c2-cafc-11e7-8241-005056bf73c0</guid><pubDate>Wed, 11 Dec 2013 18:09:33 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/abe23e78-093f-11e9-b87e-005056a964fe/w:1024/p:16x9/asterix_0.jpg">Photo: AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Paris police officers go on trial over 2020 beating of Black man</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261109-paris-police-officers-go-on-trial-over-2020-beating-of-black-man</link><description>
Three French police officers went on trial Monday over the 2020 beating of Black music producer Michel Zecler in Paris. The assault, which was captured on camera, sparked nationwide outrage and renewed scrutiny of police violence and racism in France.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/dba8d6a2-dc23-11f1-9698-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6VU4CT.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/dba8d6a2-dc23-11f1-9698-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6VU4CT.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">476e3e4a-dc24-11f1-9f04-f3d8b2b0702c</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 10:08:03 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/dba8d6a2-dc23-11f1-9698-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6VU4CT.jpg">© Thomas Samson, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Top contemporary French artist Christian Boltanski dies aged 76</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20210714-top-contemporary-french-artist-christian-boltanski-dies-aged-76</link><description>
Christian Boltanski, one of France's top contemporary artists whose multimedia works probed the meaning of mortality and memory, has died aged 76, a former museum director told AFP on Sunday.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8bb5a986-e4b7-11eb-b34d-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/e857c10696aa723e38930cb9e30ea78aa32eb150.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8bb5a986-e4b7-11eb-b34d-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/e857c10696aa723e38930cb9e30ea78aa32eb150.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b7135ce8-e4c8-11eb-89be-005056bf762b</guid><pubDate>Wed, 14 Jul 2021 18:44:40 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8bb5a986-e4b7-11eb-b34d-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/e857c10696aa723e38930cb9e30ea78aa32eb150.jpg">© Miguel Riopa, AFP</source><dc:creator>NEWS WIRES</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French students vow to continue protests despite concessions from Macron govt</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261026-macron-vows-concrete-measures-to-address-student-demands-after-unrest</link><description>
French student leaders on Monday called for more protests despite President Emmanuel Macron's pledge of  "concrete and strong" measures to address their demands after weeks of nationwide unrest. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu met with high school representatives alongside education ministers to announce follow-up action ranging from a total overhaul of higher education admissions platform Parcoursup to a cap on class sizes.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0691971e-d134-11f1-baaf-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26299412584753.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0691971e-d134-11f1-baaf-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26299412584753.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ade564d2-d134-11f1-9bc8-6d20ccb9a352</guid><pubDate>Mon, 26 Oct 2026 12:25:21 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0691971e-d134-11f1-baaf-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26299412584753.jpg">© Aurelien Morissard, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Macron says 'racist terrorist attack’ in Trappes marks turning point for France</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261023-french-prosecutors-investigate-paris-shooting-as-suspected-terror-attack</link><description>
French President Emmanuel Macron described Friday’s drive-by shooting in the western suburb of Trappes as a “terrorist and racist attack”, saying it marks a turning point for France. One person was killed and at least four people, including a 12-year-old girl, were wounded in the shooting, apparently at random. Two of the victims have immigrant backgrounds.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d100c11c-cf01-11f1-9404-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-23T164810Z-311683246-RC249OASO43C-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-SECURITY-SHOOTING-MACRON.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d100c11c-cf01-11f1-9404-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-23T164810Z-311683246-RC249OASO43C-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-SECURITY-SHOOTING-MACRON.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">72670cfa-ced0-11f1-8bc7-bb90dbb6a8a1</guid><pubDate>Fri, 23 Oct 2026 11:08:26 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d100c11c-cf01-11f1-9404-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-23T164810Z-311683246-RC249OASO43C-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-SECURITY-SHOOTING-MACRON.jpg">© Hannah McKay, Reuters</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Macron says world leaders have made 'stupid' comments on France riots based on fake AI videos</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261021-macron-says-world-leaders-have-made-stupid-comments-on-france-riots-based-on-fake-ai-videos</link><description>
French President Emmanuel Macron took aim at world leaders including US President Donald Trump for trying to exploit the riots and looting that broke out alongside peaceful demonstrations in France Saturday for their own political advantage. Another wave of demonstrations against France's worsening cost of living is planned for the coming Saturday.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/43e943ae-cd3e-11f1-a182-eb48fa034ddc/w:1024/p:16x9/c32582bbad1a265ea586d82348eed73833ee7dfb.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/43e943ae-cd3e-11f1-a182-eb48fa034ddc/w:1024/p:16x9/c32582bbad1a265ea586d82348eed73833ee7dfb.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2c665312-cd42-11f1-8dbc-290623bfb92e</guid><pubDate>Wed, 21 Oct 2026 11:48:11 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/43e943ae-cd3e-11f1-a182-eb48fa034ddc/w:1024/p:16x9/c32582bbad1a265ea586d82348eed73833ee7dfb.jpg">© Benoit Tessier, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Focus</category><title>How the French army trains for 'high-intensity' combat</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/focus/20210714-how-the-french-army-trains-for-high-intensity-conflict</link><description>
France's new military programming law increases the country's defence budget to 2 percent of GDP by 2025. It's an investment in the modernisation of equipment, but also in the training of soldiers. The aim is to teach soldiers to face an army at least as well equipped as that of France in a context of global rearmament. Our reporters Fadile Bhayat, Mandi Heshmati and Caroline Grandjean followed French troops during a "high-intensity" training exercise.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/19df5ade-e4b0-11eb-b526-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/Focus%2014%20juillet.jpeg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/19df5ade-e4b0-11eb-b526-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/Focus%2014%20juillet.jpeg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">023ce07e-e41d-11eb-a94a-005056bf762b</guid><pubDate>Wed, 14 Jul 2021 14:42:34 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Fadile BHAYAT</dc:creator></item><item><category>Perspective</category><title>'A lot of French politicians are out of touch with a large part of the population'</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/perspective/20220209-a-lot-of-french-politicians-are-out-of-touch-with-a-large-part-of-the-population</link><description>
Our guest is Fabien Truong, a sociologist, author and associate professor at the University of Paris. A former schoolteacher, he spent a decade following the lives of around 20 of his students, charting their progress from the time they took their end of school exams to when they finished their higher education. Those 10 years took in the riots that rocked France back in 2005 to the terror attacks of January 2015. He gives us his take on the French presidential election campaign, as seen from the suburbs.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/a29e27fe-89a3-11ec-8742-005056a90321/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-13035161446203b32c2451f2.07563475.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/a29e27fe-89a3-11ec-8742-005056a90321/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-13035161446203b32c2451f2.07563475.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2534ffb8-8980-11ec-8ce4-005056a97652</guid><pubDate>Wed, 09 Feb 2022 12:31:33 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Sharon GAFFNEY</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Teen wounds headmaster and teacher after opening fire at French school</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261012-french-police-arrest-14-year-old-after-two-teaching-staff-wounded-by-hunting-rifle-fire</link><description>
Two teaching staff were shot and wounded by a 14-year-old boy armed with a hunting rifle at a school in Aubagne near Marseille Monday morning, French Education Minister ‌Édouard Geffray said. Authorities said the teenager's father had been taken into custody and that there did not seem to be any link to the student protests that have swept across the country in recent weeks. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/734d60f4-a19b-11f1-ba2b-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/000-34RN2HF.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/734d60f4-a19b-11f1-ba2b-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/000-34RN2HF.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">de062bda-c61f-11f1-828c-2d5a86616301</guid><pubDate>Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:43:38 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/734d60f4-a19b-11f1-ba2b-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/000-34RN2HF.jpg">© Lou Benoist, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>'Tefal campaign': with Covid-19 monopolising voters' minds, nothing sticks</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20220209-tefal-campaign-pandemic-prudent-president-keep-french-election-race-on-the-backburner</link><description>
Presidential campaigns offer an abundance of catch phrases, whether slogans finessed by a candidate's team to deliver maximum impact or coined spontaneously on the trail. The proclamations – and gaffes – of presidential hopefuls bring texture to an election race and come to define a campaign, whether for a news cycle or forever in the history books. FRANCE 24 brings you the buzzwords of the 2022 French presidential race. In the spotlight: "Tefal campaign".
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2debad06-88f3-11ec-b463-005056a90321/w:1024/p:16x9/1280x720-Tefa-campaign.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2debad06-88f3-11ec-b463-005056a90321/w:1024/p:16x9/1280x720-Tefa-campaign.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">f4e47fa4-88f4-11ec-97bf-005056a97652</guid><pubDate>Wed, 09 Feb 2022 10:43:18 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2debad06-88f3-11ec-b463-005056a90321/w:1024/p:16x9/1280x720-Tefa-campaign.png">© FMM Graphic Studio</source><dc:creator>Tracy MCNICOLL</dc:creator></item><item><category>Spotlight</category><title>Raphaël Glucksmann, the man who wants to be French president</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/spotlight/20261011-a-profile-of-rapha%C3%ABl-glucksmann-the-man-who-wants-to-be-french-president</link><description>
Raphaël Glucksmann has won the primary to represent the French centre-left in the upcoming presidential elections, securing 66% of the vote. He now faces the challenge of building support for the centre-left in a political landscape where the far right, led by Marine Le Pen, remains a major force.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b6534792-c59a-11f1-b235-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/Raphael-Glucksmann-000-D2X49DY.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b6534792-c59a-11f1-b235-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/Raphael-Glucksmann-000-D2X49DY.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">99b61d02-c596-11f1-9bf5-777190d2ada5</guid><pubDate>Sun, 11 Oct 2026 17:50:02 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Gavin LEE</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Fire destroys Paris's oldest covered food market</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261012-fire-burns-down-paris-s-oldest-covered-food-market</link><description>
A fire "completely destroyed" Paris's historic Marché Couvert des Enfants Rouges early Monday, authorities said. The cause of the fire that swept through the capital's oldest covered food market remains unknown. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ce2023ce-c601-11f1-bf8f-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/March%C3%A9-des-Enfants-Rouges-Paris-May-2016.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ce2023ce-c601-11f1-bf8f-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/March%C3%A9-des-Enfants-Rouges-Paris-May-2016.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">c5504c60-c610-11f1-b48e-936bba59cf88</guid><pubDate>Mon, 12 Oct 2026 08:02:55 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ce2023ce-c601-11f1-bf8f-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/March%C3%A9-des-Enfants-Rouges-Paris-May-2016.jpg">© Creative Commons</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France 2022: The Choice</category><title>Battle for the French far right: Zemmour, Le Pen try to steal each other's thunder</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/france-2022-the-campaign/20220207-battle-for-the-far-right-zemmour-le-pen-fight-to-steal-each-other-s-thunder</link><description>
As France's April presidential election approaches, the campaign is getting under way in earnest. In this edition of our new show, we focus on the French Communist Party attempting a political comeback and discuss at length the battle raging between Eric Zemmour and Marine Le Pen for leadership of the French far right. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b99fd93a-885d-11ec-9917-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/XX%20NW%20OOV%20SPLIT%20LE%20PEN%20ZEMMOUR.transfer001.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b99fd93a-885d-11ec-9917-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/XX%20NW%20OOV%20SPLIT%20LE%20PEN%20ZEMMOUR.transfer001.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">6ecf0724-8861-11ec-862b-005056bf762b</guid><pubDate>Mon, 07 Feb 2022 22:00:57 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Marc PERELMAN</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French police clash with teens blockading schools as unions stage day of protests</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-french-police-clash-with-teens-blockading-schools-as-union-stage-day-of-protests</link><description>
French teenagers on Tuesday clashed with police as they kept up a blockade of high schools in cities across the country to demand better conditions and more teacher hirings. The escalating standoff came as unions staged a day of demonstrations against a cost-cutting budget drafted by Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu's embattled government.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/560db0a6-bc0e-11f1-a13f-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/07e46c53e327acb7cdaffe512bca997cd100349d.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/560db0a6-bc0e-11f1-a13f-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/07e46c53e327acb7cdaffe512bca997cd100349d.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b23ed102-bbeb-11f1-861d-cf265369200f</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 09:53:59 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/560db0a6-bc0e-11f1-a13f-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/07e46c53e327acb7cdaffe512bca997cd100349d.jpg">© Sameer Al-Doumy, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Legion of Honour: Police investigate corruption claims for France’s top award</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-legion-of-honour-police-investigate-corruption-claims-for-france-s-top-award</link><description>
French police took a top general into custody last week as part of an ongoing probe into potential bribery among the selection committee for the country’s highest decoration, the Legion of Honour. Investigations centre on possible payoffs for awards including expensive meals, holidays and thousands of euros in cash.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/202038aa-bc0f-11f1-a14f-555a0aff87a4/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17181434246649.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/202038aa-bc0f-11f1-a14f-555a0aff87a4/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17181434246649.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">cf7e5750-bc0f-11f1-9d67-9d40f7c16032</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 14:43:40 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/202038aa-bc0f-11f1-a14f-555a0aff87a4/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17181434246649.jpg">© Francois Mori, AP</source><dc:creator>Joanna YORK</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Eiffel Tower chief to step down over removal of women staff during Hindu group's visit</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-eiffel-tower-chief-to-step-down-over-removal-of-women-staff-during-hindu-group-visit-baps</link><description>
The head of the Eiffel Tower is set to step down in the wake of a controversy sparked by the removal of female workers during a private visit of the Paris landmark by members of the Hindu sect BAPS, which triggered a staff walkout earlier this month and sparked outrage in France.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1164fca6-abc0-11f1-a24c-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C79B3WE-1.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1164fca6-abc0-11f1-a24c-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C79B3WE-1.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b85f821e-bc10-11f1-89fe-7b0f1abdd3bc</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 14:22:29 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1164fca6-abc0-11f1-a24c-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C79B3WE-1.jpg">© Kenzo Tribouillard, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France's Le Pen vows to 'counterattack' after top ally Bardella hit by anti-Semitism claims</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-france-s-le-pen-vows-to-counterattack-after-top-ally-bardella-hit-by-anti-semitism-claims</link><description>
French presidential frontrunner Marine Le Pen on Tuesday denounced an attempt to "derail" her Élysée Palace run after a media report accused the head of her far-right National Rally (RN) party, Jordan Bardella, of making ant-Semitic comments in 2013. Le Pen said Bardella, who is tipped to be prime minister if she wins the presidency, had her "total confidence".
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0b97a704-bc02-11f1-8bbb-ad34ceb9e2f1</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 12:33:58 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg">© Anne-Christine Poujoulat, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France puts out massive fire that torched 42,000 hectares and smouldered for 69 days</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260928-france-puts-out-massive-fire-that-torched-42-000-hectares-and-smouldered-for-69-days</link><description>
France's largest wildfire since 1949 has been declared extinguished more than two months after it broke out in southwestern Gironde, forcing the evacuation of around 224,000 people and covering the city of Bordeaux with a thick plume of smoke. The blaze was put under control on August 1, but continued to smoulder underground for weeks.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0f68114c-bb5e-11f1-a5f5-19c8c18b5c0d</guid><pubDate>Mon, 28 Sep 2026 17:00:08 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg">© Julien De Rosa, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Far-right politician Éric Zemmour joins 2027 French presidential race</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260918-far-right-politician-%C3%A9ric-zemmour-joins-2027-french-presidential-race</link><description>
French far-right politician Éric Zemmour said on Friday that he would run in next year's presidential election, joining far-right candidate Marine Le Pen, who was runner-up to President Emmanuel Macron in the last two elections. Zemmour is campaigning on a crackdown on immigration, including a plan to expel unemployed foreigners even if they are legal residents. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2e6bcd08-b33a-11f1-b960-e76b244d1c83</guid><pubDate>Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:06:31 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg">© Emma Da Silva, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French PM vows to cut public spending by €54 billion to reduce deficit</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260918-french-pm-vows-to-cut-public-spending-by-%E2%82%AC54-billion-to-reduce-deficit</link><description>
Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said on Thursday that France will cut public spending by €54 billion next year to reduce the country's deficit. The announcement comes seven months ahead of the country's presidential election, and the government is wary of a new wave of demonstrations with a jump in global oil prices sparking concerns over the rising cost of living. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">61b975d6-b32e-11f1-ab9e-b5bbc83805db</guid><pubDate>Fri, 18 Sep 2026 07:23:41 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg">© Ludovic Marin, AFP via AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Radio France staff strike over appointment of far-right weekly editor</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260913-radio-france-staff-strike-over-appointment-of-far-right-weekly-editor</link><description>
Staff at public broadcaster Radio France began a two-day strike on Sunday over the appointment of Charles Sapin, deputy editor-in-chief at far-right weekly Valeurs Actuelles. Unions accuse Sapin of promoting far-right ideas ahead of next spring's presidential election, while management has defended the appointment in the name of pluralism.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/02d53bbe-af04-11f1-9d7b-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/e1d9fdbe2d48d1241c3b6d21d639c8533611857e.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/02d53bbe-af04-11f1-9d7b-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/e1d9fdbe2d48d1241c3b6d21d639c8533611857e.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">5ef9108e-af70-11f1-8f8f-7db7cf189a1f</guid><pubDate>Sun, 13 Sep 2026 12:44:54 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/02d53bbe-af04-11f1-9d7b-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/e1d9fdbe2d48d1241c3b6d21d639c8533611857e.jpg">© Ludovic Marin, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France apologises for diplomatic spat with US to lift block on new ambassador to Washington</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260913-france-apologises-for-diplomatic-spat-with-us-to-lift-block-on-new-ambassador-to-washington</link><description>
The French UN mission said it regretted an online post criticising a US vote at the UN General Assembly in a move that should clear the way for the new French ambassador Aurélien Lechevallier to take up his post in Washington.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8728c102-af4e-11f1-9048-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C2P7793.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8728c102-af4e-11f1-9048-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C2P7793.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">9c8e07e2-af4d-11f1-8c62-892c781611bd</guid><pubDate>Sun, 13 Sep 2026 09:01:17 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8728c102-af4e-11f1-9048-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C2P7793.jpg">© Ludovic Marin, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

      <description><p>CEO reportedly ‌had close relationship ‌with a Chinese businesswoman who passed information to ‌Beijing</p><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/nvidia">Nvidia</a> said ⁠on Sunday it “is initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/oct/29/nvidia-ceo-targeted-chinese-spy">target</a> of a foreign intelligence effort”.</p><p>The <a href="https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/29/us/politics/nvidia-china-jensen-huang-trump.html">New York Times reported</a> in ​October that <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/donaldtrump">Donald Trump</a> had been briefed last year on intelligence that Huang ‌had a close relationship ‌with a <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/china">Chinese</a> businesswoman who passed information to ‌Beijing.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/08/nvidia-jensen-huang-investigation">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 00:25:28 GMT</pubDate>
      <guid>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/08/nvidia-jensen-huang-investigation</guid>
      <media:content width="140" url="https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/3fc6a5d68684a58fece0294bce9094ed76072ecd/2488_14_5430_4347/master/5430.jpg?width=140&quality=85&auto=format&fit=max&s=57b1a4b39c9e4d81da1942f21f2da458">

      <description><p>Polling done for the Guardian shows plummeting support from a former key constituency of Donald Trump’s base</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/community/live/2026/nov/05/what-happens-after-the-blue-wave-our-reporters-answer-your-midterm-election-results-questions">Q&amp;A: Ask your questions about Democrats’ win in the midterms</a></p></li></ul><p>Polling conducted by the Harris Poll for the Guardian before the election shows just how angry voters were and points to one key reason Republicans lost so badly: plummeting support from rural voters, once a key constituency of Donald Trump’s base.</p><p>Over the summer, 95% of Americans indicated they believed there was an <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/jul/07/cost-of-living-poll-groceries-gas">affordability crisis</a>, particularly because of steep gas and grocery prices.       <link>https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/04/us-dollar-slides-democrats-midterm-election-win-growth-fears</link>
      <description><p>Government bond yields fall while initial fears ease over impact of election results on world’s biggest economy</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/live/2026/nov/04/midterm-elections-results-senate-house-michigan-maine-mississippi-latest-updates">US midterm elections – live updates</a></p></li><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/04/explainer-midterms-trump-us-global-economy-markets">After US midterms, what will lame-duck Trump mean for global economy?</a></p></li></ul><p>US stocks have surged as investors digest the Democrats’ victories in the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/us-midterm-elections-2026">midterm elections</a>, lifted by hopes that <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/donaldtrump">Donald Trump</a>’s turbulent policymaking would be restrained and shaking off initial fears about the impact on growth in the world’s largest economy.</p><p>The Dow Jones rose close to 3%, its best day in over a year, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq and the benchmark S&amp;P 500 gained about 1.5% each when markets closed on Wednesday afternoon, turning around overnight falls in US stock futures after the news that the Democratic party <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/live/2026/nov/03/midterm-election-results-live-updates">won control</a> of the Senate and the House of Representatives.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/04/us-dollar-slides-democrats-midterm-election-win-growth-fears">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Trump may have lost but don’t bet Democrats can fix the economy</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/07/democrats-economy-affordability-crisis</link>
      <description><p>There’s not much they can do over the next couple of years to alleviate angry voters’ stress over prices</p><p>It was the economy, again. Although Donald Trump largely ignored it, voters’ acute concerns over the rising cost of living fuelled a political upheaval for the ages that is likely to deliver the biggest swing toward Democrats since Watergate, granting them the largest House majority in nearly four decades alongside their biggest edge in the Senate since 2008.</p><p>Still, having come to power promising to restore affordability, the new crop of Democrats are soon to discover that there is not much they can do over the next couple of years to alleviate angry voters’ stress over pricey gas and groceries, exorbitant mortgages and unaffordable healthcare.</p><p>Eduardo Porter is a journalist focused on economics and politics.       <description><p>A layoff and a leap of faith convinced Katie Teixeira she had what it takes to run her own business</p><p>In 2010, Katie Teixeira adopted a kitten found all alone in an abandoned house. The kitten – so tiny she fit in the palm of Teixeira’s hand – needed to be bottle-fed every few hours. For weeks, Teixeira set her alarm for middle-of-the-night feedings and drove home on her lunch break to care for the kitten she named Milo.       <title>The survival of American democracy depends on taxing billionaires</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/27/democracy-tax-billionaires</link>
      <description><p>It is essential not just to fund the public goods the nation needs, it is indispensable to restore a sense of fairness</p><p>Money doesn’t buy happiness, we’re told. Even some economists agree. The Nobel prize-winning economists Daniel Kahneman and Angus Deaton once <a href="https://www.pnas.org/doi/full/10.1073/pnas.1011492107">proposed that</a> rising income increased people’s emotional wellbeing only up to a ceiling of about $115,000 in today’s money.</p><p>They probably hadn’t met many billionaires. The ultra-rich may not pursue happiness in the joyful sense of the word. But they will try every trick in the book to hang on to their stash and woe betide the tax authority that tries to lay a finger on their treasure.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/27/democracy-tax-billionaires">Continue reading...</a></description>

The latest information, news and events in France, Europe and around the world.</description><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/</link><lastBuildDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 14:33:10 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>France</category><title>'I still have nightmares': victim of police violence seeks justice six years on</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261109-i-still-have-nightmares-victim-of-police-violence-seeks-justice-six-years-on-michel-zecler</link><description>
Three French police officers are to go on trial on Monday over the brutal beating of black music producer Michel Zecler in Paris in 2020 – a case that sparked nationwide outrage over police violence and racism.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/88ce45b6-dba1-11f1-91d2-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/FRANCE-JUSTICE-MICHEL-ZECLER.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/88ce45b6-dba1-11f1-91d2-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/FRANCE-JUSTICE-MICHEL-ZECLER.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0aa97116-dc27-11f1-890c-17b2c492ee48</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 14:29:18 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/88ce45b6-dba1-11f1-91d2-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/FRANCE-JUSTICE-MICHEL-ZECLER.jpg">AFP - JOEL SAGET</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Mélenchon bets on radical change as French presidential race takes shape</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261109-m%C3%A9lenchon-bets-on-radical-change-as-french-presidential-race-takes-shape</link><description>
Leader of the hard-left France Unbowed party, Jean-Luc Mélenchon has vowed to pursue an uncompromising programme of radical change as he bids for the French presidency in 2027. This sets up a potentially decisive confrontation with far-right leader Marine Le Pen, despite warnings that his divisive politics could ultimately hand her victory.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/28b90688-dc1f-11f1-84be-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/M%C3%A9lenchon-7-November-2026.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/28b90688-dc1f-11f1-84be-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/M%C3%A9lenchon-7-November-2026.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">273d195c-dc1a-11f1-8d60-5f29074843e0</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 13:01:32 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/28b90688-dc1f-11f1-84be-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/M%C3%A9lenchon-7-November-2026.jpg">©  KENZO TRIBOUILLARD / AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Drop in French food bank collection as rising cost of living hits donations</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261109-drop-in-french-food-bank-collection-as-rising-cost-of-living-hits-donations</link><description>
France’s annual food bank collection has gathered less than expected in the face of the rising cost of living which has left people with less money to spend on donations. The three-day campaign, which ended on Sunday, aimed to collect enough food to provide the equivalent of 20 million meals.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b1392996-dbc2-11f1-af3e-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/000-32TL9GD-1.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b1392996-dbc2-11f1-af3e-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/000-32TL9GD-1.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b7b3dffa-dc2b-11f1-8a7f-0f7ff0c2412a</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 12:09:22 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b1392996-dbc2-11f1-af3e-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/000-32TL9GD-1.jpg">© Mehdi Fedouach/AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French MPs weigh debate on banning conservative TV channel as petition tops 1m</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261109-french-mps-to-weigh-debate-on-banning-conservative-tv-channel-as-petition-tops-1m-cnews</link><description>
A petition calling for French television channel CNews, often compared to US broadcaster Fox News, to be shut down has received over a million signatures, two days before lawmakers meet to consider whether a ban should be debated in parliament.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b0dc3b9c-dba8-11f1-b566-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D66Z6FA.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b0dc3b9c-dba8-11f1-b566-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D66Z6FA.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">19210fc8-dc0a-11f1-bd4e-25468b64d7d5</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 06:52:14 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b0dc3b9c-dba8-11f1-b566-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D66Z6FA.jpg">© Anne-Christine Poujoulat/AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Unions vow to keep pressure on French government after fourth wave of protests</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261108-unions-vow-to-keep-pressure-on-french-government-after-fourth-wave-of-protests</link><description>
Education union chiefs on Sunday vowed to maintain pressure on the government after student organisations called for another day of nationwide strikes and demonstrations on Tuesday.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a57fc52e-db63-11f1-b306-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/prote.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a57fc52e-db63-11f1-b306-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/prote.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">36cb7bb6-dac6-11f1-b148-e9346ba72bac</guid><pubDate>Sun, 08 Nov 2026 11:00:57 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a57fc52e-db63-11f1-b306-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/prote.jpg">AP Photo/Emma Da Silva - Emma Da Silva</source><dc:creator>Paul Myers</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>French students vow to continue protests</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/video/20261107-french-students-vow-to-continue-protests-paris</link><description>
French pupils and students are protesting and blockading schools over poor conditions and a university admissions system (Parcoursup) seen as over-selective and opaque. Despite recent concessions by the government, students at Hélène Boucher high school in Paris say they'll continue, even after riot place were sent to break their blockade.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bed31678-c945-11f1-84f0-638c1c1f5fd6/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-16T075646Z-1864054812-RC274OA7GQ58-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST-2.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bed31678-c945-11f1-84f0-638c1c1f5fd6/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-16T075646Z-1864054812-RC274OA7GQ58-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST-2.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">8c9b5ff0-dab9-11f1-a45a-31b57fcb4ae5</guid><pubDate>Sat, 07 Nov 2026 15:02:47 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France braces for second day of protests within 48 hours</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261107-france-braces-for-second-day-of-protests-within-48-hours</link><description>
Hundreds of thousands of people were expected to take to the streets on Saturday for a day of protests over the poor conditions in schools and the rising cost of living.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fb2ec67e-d9cd-11f1-a5cc-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T151241Z-1266580735-RC2OHOAVSIEZ-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fb2ec67e-d9cd-11f1-a5cc-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T151241Z-1266580735-RC2OHOAVSIEZ-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">33ad1cbc-da96-11f1-8df4-1da1eb33321e</guid><pubDate>Sat, 07 Nov 2026 12:10:04 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fb2ec67e-d9cd-11f1-a5cc-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T151241Z-1266580735-RC2OHOAVSIEZ-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">REUTERS - Hannah McKay</source><dc:creator>Paul Myers</dc:creator></item><item><category>Spotlight on France</category><title>Podcast: France's student protests and how they fuelled a larger social movement</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/podcasts/spotlight-on-france/20261106-podcast-france-s-student-protests-and-how-they-fuelled-a-larger-social-movement-may-68</link><description>
A look at France's high school protests and how they have fed into an ongoing social movement. What are the students protesting against? What impact has the police crackdown had? How has the government reacted? And a comparison with student movements of the past.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/884fdc42-d9cd-11f1-80bf-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/episode-spotlight-on-france-episode-152-peach-pink.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/884fdc42-d9cd-11f1-80bf-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/episode-spotlight-on-france-episode-152-peach-pink.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">bcd965aa-d9cd-11f1-b272-af07f9a85ea6</guid><pubDate>Fri, 06 Nov 2026 15:29:10 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Sarah Elzas</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French lawyers to sue interior minister over 'mutilation' of young protesters</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261106-french-lawyers-to-sue-interior-minister-over-mutilation-of-young-protesters</link><description>
Lawyers representing at least 18 people injured during protests in France in recent weeks say they intend to file a complaint against Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez over his alleged responsibility for police brutality.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/ad744280-bea5-11f1-8056-578a4b968fd6/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-02T104258Z-1424347954-RC2XUNAITHZX-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/ad744280-bea5-11f1-8056-578a4b968fd6/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-02T104258Z-1424347954-RC2XUNAITHZX-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">dba18ef0-d9e5-11f1-863b-f351e1b5079d</guid><pubDate>Fri, 06 Nov 2026 14:39:42 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/ad744280-bea5-11f1-8056-578a4b968fd6/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-02T104258Z-1424347954-RC2XUNAITHZX-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">REUTERS - Nacho Doce</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>'AI cannot do everything': bullying experts warn against confiding in chatbots</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261106-one-quarter-of-young-bullying-victims-turning-to-ai-for-help-study-finds</link><description>
As a growing number of victims turn to artificial intelligence for help, experts warn that, while a virtual confidante can offer temporary relief, the focus must be on prevention and support.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/808c3c9c-cd36-11f1-b7ef-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/yamu-jay-school-bullying-9060270.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/808c3c9c-cd36-11f1-b7ef-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/yamu-jay-school-bullying-9060270.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">71185a8c-d797-11f1-a35f-45b5729425b2</guid><pubDate>Fri, 06 Nov 2026 09:35:34 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/808c3c9c-cd36-11f1-b7ef-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/yamu-jay-school-bullying-9060270.jpg">© pixabay / Yamu_Jay</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Latest figures show domestic violence still major problem in France</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261106-chilling-figures-show-domestic-violence-still-major-problem-in-france</link><description>
French authorities recorded 285,000 victims of domestic violence in 2025, mostly women, representing a 5 percent increase in a year. It comes as lawmakers debate a new law against sexual and gender-based violence that is due to be finalised at the beginning of 2027.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fb36a16c-43a7-11f1-8f1d-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26090564561960.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fb36a16c-43a7-11f1-8f1d-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26090564561960.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">77dc943a-d92e-11f1-90a5-5193511bd582</guid><pubDate>Fri, 06 Nov 2026 06:08:15 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fb36a16c-43a7-11f1-8f1d-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26090564561960.jpg">© Andreea Alexandru / AP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>‘We’ll get them’: Macron’s private comments on rivals revealed in new book</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261105-we-ll-get-them-macron-s-private-comments-on-rivals-revealed-in-new-book</link><description>
Private messages exchanged between French President Emmanuel Macron and journalist Françoise Degois over two years have been published in a new book, revealing his views on political rivals, the rise of the far right and his own leadership. The president reportedly learnt of the book’s existence just three days before its release.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fb95d9d2-d896-11f1-b8ef-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP22177506677032-1.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fb95d9d2-d896-11f1-b8ef-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP22177506677032-1.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ed7d8d46-d8f9-11f1-8648-c35846abfa7a</guid><pubDate>Thu, 05 Nov 2026 16:07:25 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fb95d9d2-d896-11f1-b8ef-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP22177506677032-1.jpg">© AP - Susan Walsh </source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French prosecutors investigate €100m cyberattack on Crédit Mutuel banking group</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261105-french-prosecutors-investigate-%E2%82%AC100m-cyberattack-on-cr%C3%A9dit-mutuel-banking-group</link><description>
French prosecutors have opened an investigation into a sophisticated cyberattack on Crédit Mutuel Arkéa involving fraudulent transfers estimated at around €100 million, as the Brittany-based banking group races to recover the stolen funds.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a8dda14a-d907-11f1-a6f6-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/Cr%C3%A9dit-Mutuel-Ark%C3%A9a.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a8dda14a-d907-11f1-a6f6-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/Cr%C3%A9dit-Mutuel-Ark%C3%A9a.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">d4c86e50-d8f5-11f1-8292-031c66ea2070</guid><pubDate>Thu, 05 Nov 2026 12:31:26 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a8dda14a-d907-11f1-a6f6-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/Cr%C3%A9dit-Mutuel-Ark%C3%A9a.jpg">AFP - FRED TANNEAU</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>MPs unanimously reject 2027 French budget as political deadlock continues</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261105-french-mps-unanimously-reject-2027-budget-as-political-deadlock-deepens</link><description>
France's National Assembly has overwhelmingly rejected the government's draft budget for 2027 after MPs from across the political spectrum voted against a heavily amended version of the legislation, sending the bill to the Senate in its original form and setting the stage for another round of difficult negotiations.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/8c795750-c2d3-11f1-9d03-c55799ef8309/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D2DV9WP.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/8c795750-c2d3-11f1-9d03-c55799ef8309/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D2DV9WP.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">94610092-d8ec-11f1-83cc-05d8d1a87801</guid><pubDate>Thu, 05 Nov 2026 08:19:33 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/8c795750-c2d3-11f1-9d03-c55799ef8309/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D2DV9WP.jpg">© AFP/Dimitar Dilkoff</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Mass protests sweep France as workers and students demand higher pay and funding</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261105-french-unions-join-forces-for-nationwide-strike-as-protests-intensify</link><description>
Hundreds of thousands of people took to the streets across France on Thursday as workers, students and pensioners joined nationwide strikes and demonstrations demanding higher wages, action on the cost of living and better public services. Nearly 1.6 million people joined the marches, including 350,000 in Paris, the CGT union said. The Interior Ministry gave a much lower nationwide estimate of around 600,000.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/3e9309cc-d936-11f1-b338-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26309546527183.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/3e9309cc-d936-11f1-b338-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26309546527183.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">d1ac4db2-d847-11f1-8e8e-b39696b484d3</guid><pubDate>Thu, 05 Nov 2026 07:11:27 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/3e9309cc-d936-11f1-b338-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26309546527183.jpg">© AP Photo/Thibault Camus</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Students blockade dozens of high schools in France before nationwide strike</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261103-students-blockade-dozens-of-high-schools-in-france-before-nationwide-strike</link><description>
Students blockaded dozens of high schools across France on Tuesday to maintain pressure on the government over education reforms as trade unions prepared for a nationwide strike later this week.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/21c9ae56-d6d2-11f1-afea-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D64N373.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/21c9ae56-d6d2-11f1-afea-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D64N373.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0f797ebc-d75d-11f1-9716-917a4357a158</guid><pubDate>Tue, 03 Nov 2026 12:20:54 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/21c9ae56-d6d2-11f1-afea-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D64N373.jpg">© Matthieu Rondel / AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Calls mount to ban French TV channel following racist killing</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261102-calls-mount-to-ban-french-tv-channel-after-racist-killing</link><description>
A petition urging that a French television channel be taken off air gained traction on Monday, after accusations that far-right views it aired contributed to the racist killing of a black man. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/25b7c5b8-d6c6-11f1-947b-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D4Y89JC.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/25b7c5b8-d6c6-11f1-947b-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D4Y89JC.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">8d41d30a-d6d4-11f1-996a-c9565a8083a3</guid><pubDate>Mon, 02 Nov 2026 15:54:59 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/25b7c5b8-d6c6-11f1-947b-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D4Y89JC.jpg">AFP - SIMON WOHLFAHRT</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France braces for fresh protests as students to resume school blockades</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261102-france-braces-for-fresh-protests-as-students-to-resume-school-blockades</link><description>
France is readying for another week of protests after the head of a student group said a campaign of high school blockades would restart Monday, ahead of a nationwide day of strikes and protests on Thursday.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/8bf6d858-c15b-11f1-967e-b942c38e4bd7/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-06T073959Z-1661401214-RC2JXNALODN9-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/8bf6d858-c15b-11f1-967e-b942c38e4bd7/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-06T073959Z-1661401214-RC2JXNALODN9-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">fe830974-d5e6-11f1-94c2-0ddebd68042b</guid><pubDate>Mon, 02 Nov 2026 07:09:12 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/8bf6d858-c15b-11f1-967e-b942c38e4bd7/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-06T073959Z-1661401214-RC2JXNALODN9-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">REUTERS - Tom Nicholson</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Five British anti-immigration activists arrested in northern France</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261101-five-british-anti-migrant-ultra-right-activists-arrested-in-north-of-france</link><description>
French police say they've arrested five British far-right activists found carrying tear gas bombs, as they were filming themselves harassing migrants near the northern Channel port of Dunkirk.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/31d0c036-4bf0-11ec-abc5-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/AP21324042369756.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/31d0c036-4bf0-11ec-abc5-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/AP21324042369756.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ed941388-d5fa-11f1-9c92-8d270bd12c5c</guid><pubDate>Sun, 01 Nov 2026 14:18:30 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/31d0c036-4bf0-11ec-abc5-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/AP21324042369756.jpg">© AP Photo/Louis Witter</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France launches 'attempted murder' probe after petrol bomb attack on police</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261101-france-launches-attempted-murder-probe-after-petrol-bomb-attack-on-police</link><description>
France has launched an attempted murder investigation after petrol bombs were thrown at security forces during a weekend protest in Paris, prosecutors told AFP on Sunday.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/f2d8ffc4-d565-11f1-aa94-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/84b0f9d200b86233f18834393d966b98a1b52af4.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/f2d8ffc4-d565-11f1-aa94-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/84b0f9d200b86233f18834393d966b98a1b52af4.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">c8e54780-d5f7-11f1-8f9a-d78b8e884648</guid><pubDate>Sun, 01 Nov 2026 13:26:02 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/f2d8ffc4-d565-11f1-aa94-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/84b0f9d200b86233f18834393d966b98a1b52af4.jpg">© Sameer AL-DOUMY / AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France sees third weekend of protests as youth-led rallies sweep Europe</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261031-france-sees-third-weekend-of-protests-as-youth-led-rallies-sweep-europe</link><description>
Hundreds of thousands of mostly young protesters, some dressed as clowns and witches for Halloween, took to the streets across France on Saturday in a third weekend of demonstrations over living costs and education. Police fired tear gas in Paris after clashes broke out at the end of the march. Youth rallies were also held in Germany and Italy.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/316d67d0-d54c-11f1-a9e9-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-31T161057Z-1540280500-RC2FEOAN304W-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/316d67d0-d54c-11f1-a9e9-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-31T161057Z-1540280500-RC2FEOAN304W-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">1eff833e-d543-11f1-b06a-ffc2e7fd2caa</guid><pubDate>Sat, 31 Oct 2026 17:46:47 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/316d67d0-d54c-11f1-a9e9-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-31T161057Z-1540280500-RC2FEOAN304W-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">REUTERS - Manon Cruz</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Minister warns of risk of violence ahead of Halloween 'night of darkness' protests</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261031-minister-warns-of-risk-of-violence-ahead-of-halloween-night-of-darkness-protests</link><description>
With student groups and Yellow Vest activists set for a third consecutive weekend of demonstrations against poor conditions in schools and the rising cost of living, Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez has said 70,000 police officers and gendarmes will be deployed across France on Saturday. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/69f81ba6-d450-11f1-b62e-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D3KU3H6.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/69f81ba6-d450-11f1-b62e-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D3KU3H6.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">4b9a3b5e-d445-11f1-9e6a-5f14884e5daf</guid><pubDate>Sat, 31 Oct 2026 08:34:58 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/69f81ba6-d450-11f1-b62e-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D3KU3H6.jpg">AFP - CHRISTOPHE ARCHAMBAULT</source><dc:creator>Paul Myers</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>What is France's 'great replacement' conspiracy theory and how is it spreading?</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261030-what-is-france-s-great-replacement-conspiracy-theory-and-how-is-it-spreading</link><description>
A week after shootings in the Paris suburbs of Trappes and La Verrière that are being investigated as a terrorist attack motivated by race, the mayor of Trappes has called for the "great replacement" theory – which claims white French people are being deliberately replaced by non-Europeans – to be banned by law.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/73ca4158-d483-11f1-8054-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/AP24094743230701.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/73ca4158-d483-11f1-8054-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/AP24094743230701.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ec23f022-d44c-11f1-9a4a-8d24f1bca529</guid><pubDate>Fri, 30 Oct 2026 17:47:01 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/73ca4158-d483-11f1-8054-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/AP24094743230701.jpg">AP - Laurent Cipriani</source><dc:creator>Alison Hird</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French dockworkers strike over budget measures and militarisation of ports</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261030-french-dockworkers-strike-over-budget-measures-and-militarisation-of-ports-arms-war</link><description>
French ports are expected to be almost completely shut down on Friday as dockworkers join a 24-hour strike across 22 countries to protest against the use of ports for arms exports. French workers are also demonstrating against proposed measures in the country's draft budget. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/d25f3b80-1569-11ec-a3d6-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/000_Par2521606.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/d25f3b80-1569-11ec-a3d6-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/000_Par2521606.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">e5d1f3dc-d432-11f1-82fd-876b12b9de9a</guid><pubDate>Fri, 30 Oct 2026 08:19:09 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/d25f3b80-1569-11ec-a3d6-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/000_Par2521606.jpg">AFP - ROBERT FRANCOIS</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Paris suburb shooting suspect 'targeted Muslims, Africans or North Africans'</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261029-paris-suburb-shooting-suspect-targeted-muslims-africans-or-north-africans</link><description>
The man being held over the shootings which took place last Friday in the Paris suburbs of Trappes and La Verrière – which left one man dead and several people wounded, including an 11-year-old girl – has said he specifically targeted people of Muslim, African or North African appearance, anti-terrorism investigators revealed on Thursday.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b8499e0a-cff6-11f1-a35a-4b25c96ec90e/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D4AX6UN.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b8499e0a-cff6-11f1-a35a-4b25c96ec90e/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D4AX6UN.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">59bc4dbe-d38f-11f1-83b1-93c98f0401df</guid><pubDate>Thu, 29 Oct 2026 14:46:06 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b8499e0a-cff6-11f1-a35a-4b25c96ec90e/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D4AX6UN.jpg">© Simon Wohlfahrt / AFP</source><dc:creator>Paul Myers</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

      <title>Felix Nmecha’s faith is forcing Borussia Dortmund into an uncomfortable debate</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/09/felix-nmecha-faith-borussia-dortmund-debate-bundesliga</link>
      <description><p>Midfielder’s spectacular strikes rescued a frustrating day, only for celebrations to reignite dialogue that has followed him through his career</p><p>It was just what they needed at just the right time. For a tricky first half and beyond, Elversberg had been a stone in Borussia Dortmund’s shoe, the promoted side not just keeping the home team at bay but keeping them honest, nourishing ambitions of their own. “The fatigue was clearly visible,” said the sporting director, Ole Book, to Sky after a week which had <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/31/european-football-harry-kane-bayern-munich-borussia-dortmund-milan-inter-barcelona">contained </a><em><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/31/european-football-harry-kane-bayern-munich-borussia-dortmund-milan-inter-barcelona">Der Klassiker</a></em> in Munich and a hard-fought Champions League victory over Betis. “We were a bit too focused on managing the game, which was understandable.”</p><p>Enter Felix Nmecha. BVB have enjoyed a largely excellent start to the season, are unbeaten and level on points with Bayern Munich at the top; Bayern lead, unsurprisingly, thanks to their superior goal difference. It is a gap which has been widened by Dortmund being far from prolific, a facet which looked as if it might undercut their efforts to roll over their visitors on Saturday, especially in the absence of the injured centre-forward Serhou Guirassy.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/09/felix-nmecha-faith-borussia-dortmund-debate-bundesliga">Continue reading...</a></description>

    <item>
      <title>Football comes together across Spain to honour Jesús de Miguel: ‘We’ve seen how fragile life is’</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/09/football-comes-together-spain-honour-jesus-de-miguel-tenerife</link>
      <description><p>Across La Liga and beyond this weekend, footballers took to the field knowing it could have been them</p><p>In the final few minutes before stepping into the arena once more, heading out for his 199th Osasuna match on Saturday evening, the man who has scored more first division goals <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/feb/17/osasuna-ante-budimir-real-madrid-bellingham-la-liga">than anyone in their history</a> stopped his teammates for a moment and told them what it meant to wear the shirt. “This is very important,” Ante Budimir began as the dressing room, their sanctuary, fell silent around him. “We don’t have this shirt today for the sake of it. He was not chosen, and nor are we. It could have happened to anyone, anyone. Let us go knowing that we’re grateful to be on the pitch: playing, watching, warming up, sitting on the bench, whatever it may be. Boys, we were not chosen: not us, not him. Let us go, gratefully. Without thought. We have a grand day before us.”</p><p>With that, Osasuna’s players turned left out of the room, where they were joined in the tunnel by footballers from Athletic Club, rivals from the north, and together they went out past the little shrine of Saint Fermin on to the field. They carried white lilies and all wore the same white shirts with a No 9 on the back, a black ribbon and the name of Jesús de Miguel, the Tenerife striker <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/03/tenerife-footballer-jesus-de-miguel-hospital-collision">who died after a collision on the pitch</a> five days earlier at the age of 30. At almost exactly the same time, 2,000km away to the west, Tenerife’s squad were walking out at the Heliodoro Rodríguez López in Santa Cruz. They did not have anyone alongside them, wore black suits not white shirts and did not have a game to play either, not this week.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/09/football-comes-together-spain-honour-jesus-de-miguel-tenerife">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>The City striker hit a WSL hat-trick for the ninth time while Eva Olid’s United have found defensive stability</p><p>Not only did Khadija “Bunny” Shaw score a record-extending ninth WSL hat-trick, she scored a “perfect hat-trick” for the fourth time in the competition, something nobody else has managed more than once. Against West Ham the Jamaica striker opened the scoring with her left foot, headed home her second off the underside of the crossbar and tucked in her third with her right foot late on. It helped her side towards a 5-0 win that opened up a two-point gap at the top of the table and stretched Shaw’s lead in the race to be the top division’s top scorer to a five-goal advantage over her nearest challenger, Océane Hurtré. Can anybody stop her relentless pursuit of another Golden Boot?
